newsitem.title: UK: Focus - Oil prices slide as U.S. stocks mount.
newsitem.headline: Focus - Oil prices slide as U.S. stocks mount.

text.p: Oil prices eased lower on Wednesday on news of rising stocks in the United States, the world's key import market .
Oil markets have been recently treading water in anticipation of a surge in U.S. gasoline demand to fuel the summer driving season.
But the country's leading oil industry association said on Wednesday that domestic gasoline supplies are expected to be more than sufficient to fuel even the most bullish forecasts for demand growth.

"In our view, gasoline supply has the potential to grow enough this summer in order to accommodate even the higher 2.5 percent rate of growth suggested by our upper-bound demand estimate," the American Petroleum Institute (API) said in its annual outlook for the summer.

World benchmark Brent futures for June delivery were 14 cents down at $18.00 a barrel in London at 1630 GMT, while prompt crude futures on the New York Mercentile Exchange (NYMEX) were 27 cents lower at $19.56.

API oil stocks data released after the close of business on Tuesday for the week ended April 11 showed that gasoline stocks increased by 3.6 million barrels compared to a one to two million barrel decline expected by traders.
The data implied that demand fell to a seasonally weak 7.3 million barrels per day (bpd) compared to 8.1 million bpd the week before.
"The data was a surprise because people were looking for seasonal demand for gasoline and not getting it which is a disappointment," said Victor Yu, vice president of brokers Refco Inc. in New York.
Crude oil stocks rose for the sixth consecutive week and are now 11.3 million barrels higher than a year ago in the U.S. Gulf Coast refining belt where demand is concentrated.

Inventory levels for distillates -- which include heating oil -- also defied traders' expectations by swelling more than 2.5 million barrels despite unseasonably cold weather in the key North East market.

Some traders expected a combination of the bearish stocks data and an easing of tensions between key crude exporter Iran and the West to push oil prices back towards the nine-month lows posted last week.
